sect1.title: GStreamer-&gstreamer-version;
sect1.sect2:
Introduction to GStreamer
GStreamer is a multimedia framework that enables applications to share a common set of plugins for tasks such as video encoding and decoding, audio encoding and decoding, audio and video filters, audio visualisation, web streaming and anything else that streams in real-time or otherwise. This page provides most of the set of packages for ease of installation as they mostly have the same instructions.

sect2.title: Downloading GStreamer
sect2.para: First create a list of files that will be downloaded:
To download the needed files using , use the following commands:

screen.userinput: mkdir gstreamer && cd gstreamer && grep -v '^#' ../gstreamer-&gstreamer-version;-list | wget -i- -c \ -B &gstreamer-dl;/

sect1.sect2:
Installation of GStreamer
&as_root;
First do a test to see if GStreamer is installed, and if it is, remove the previous installation
Removal of previous installation is required or else processes may hang or not function properly due to mixed versions being installed. :
pkgconf gstreamer-1.0 if test x"$?" = x"0"; then as_root rm -rvf /usr/bin/gst-* /usr/{lib,libexec}/gstreamer-1.0 fi
Now start a subshell that will exit on error:
bash -e
Install all of the packages by running the following commands:
for package in $(grep -v '^#' ../gstreamer-&gstreamer-version;-list) do package=$(basename "$package") packagedir=${package%.tar.?z*} echo "Building $packagedir" tar -xf $package pushd $packagedir
case $packagedir in gstreamer-[0-9]* ) extraflags="-D gst_debug=false" ;; gst-plugins-base-[0-9]* ) extraflags="--wrap-mode=nodownload" ;; gst-plugins-bad-[0-9]* ) extraflags="-D gpl=enabled -D gsm=disabled" ;; gst-plugins-ugly-[0-9]* ) extraflags="-D gpl=enabled" ;; * ) extraflags= ;; esac
mkdir build cd build meson setup --prefix=/usr \ --buildtype=release \ $(echo $extraflags) \ .. ninja as_root ninja install popd rm -rf $packagedir done
Finally, exit the shell that was started earlier:
exit

sect2.title: lib32 Installation of GStreamer
sect2.para: First do a test to see if GStreamer is installed, and if it is, remove the previous installation:

screen.userinput: i686-pc-linux-gnu-pkg-config gstreamer-1.0 if test x"$?" = x"0"; then as_root rm -rvf /usr/lib32/gstreamer-1.0 fi

sect2.para: Now start a subshell that will exit on error:
Install all of the packages by running the following commands:

screen.userinput:
for package in $(grep -v '^#' ../gstreamer-&gstreamer-version;-list) do package=$(basename "$package") packagedir=${package%.tar.?z*} echo "Building lib32-$packagedir" tar -xf $package pushd $packagedir
case $packagedir in gstreamer-[0-9]* ) extraflags="-D gst_debug=false" ;; gst-plugins-base-[0-9]* ) extraflags="--wrap-mode=nodownload -D qt5=disabled" ;; gst-plugins-good-[0-9]* ) extraflags="$([ -f /usr/lib32/libmp3lame.so ] || echo "-D lame=disabled")" extraflags+=" -D qt5=disabled -D qt6=disabled" ;; gst-plugins-bad-[0-9]* ) extraflags="-D gpl=enabled -D gsm=disabled" ;; gst-plugins-ugly-[0-9]* ) extraflags="-D gpl=enabled" ;; * ) extraflags= ;; esac
mkdir build cd build meson setup --prefix=/usr \ --buildtype=release \ --cross-file=lib32 \ $(echo $extraflags) \ .. ninja DESTDIR=$PWD/DESTDIR ninja install as_root cp -vR DESTDIR/usr/lib32/* /usr/lib32 rm -rf DESTDIR popd rm -rf $packagedir as_root /sbin/ldconfig done

sect2.para: Finally, exit the shell that was started earlier:

sect1.sect2:
Command Explanations
&options-meson;
&meson-buildtype-release;
-D gpl=enabled: Without this switch, plugins with dependencies on (A)GPL licensed libraries are not built.
-D gsm=disabled: This switch disables linking to the GSM library if it is installed, as it will cause a build failure.
-D qt{5,6}=disabled: On a multilib system, while Qt-5 or Qt-6 may be installed, it is far less likely for them to be installed for lib32. meson falsely detects them being installed if 64-bit installations are detected, which leads to linker errors. If you have installed lib32-Qt-{5,6}, remove these parameters.
$([ -f /usr/lib32/libmp3lame.so ] ...: This command searches for a library from one of the recommended dependencies, and if it can't find the library, the command invokes -D lame=disabled to disable LAME support for the 32-bit build as meson can't detect if it is the right architecture or not.
